articles.excerpt: This tutorial was written with AI assistance from the project's official documentation. Verification status is stated at the end of the article. Gitea is a single-binary Git service written in Go. It…
articles.body: This tutorial was written with AI assistance from the project's official documentation. Verification status is stated at the end of the article. What Gitea does and what it needs Gitea is a single-binary Git service written in Go. It bundles repository hosting, pull requests, issue tracking, wikis, a package registry, and a GitHub Actions-compatible CI runner into one process. The official image is gitea/gitea , and the container exposes two ports: 3000 for HTTP and 22 for SSH-based Git operations. Gitea stores almost everything in two places: the SQL database (SQLite by default, or PostgreSQL/MySQL) and the GITEA_WORK_DIR directory, which holds repositories, attachments, LFS objects, and the app.ini config.

There are keys for five providers in a dozen places, it is hard to say what last month's spend bought, and every team has quietly picked the strongest model for everything, because nobody was ever told off for an answer that was too good. articles.title: Moodle behind TLS offload needs $CFG->sslproxy
articles.excerpt: Moodle™ sees the request PHP received. If nginx, HAProxy, an F5, or Cloudflare terminates TLS and the PHP pool speaks HTTP on localhost, $_SERVER['HTTPS'] is empty. $CFG->wwwroot is still https://lms.…
articles.body: Moodle™ sees the request PHP received. If nginx, HAProxy, an F5, or Cloudflare terminates TLS and the PHP pool speaks HTTP on localhost, $_SERVER['HTTPS'] is empty. $CFG->wwwroot is still https://lms.example.org . Login then 302-loops, cookies drop the Secure flag, and generated URLs flip to http:// . config-dist.php names the switch: // Enable when using external SSL appliance for performance reasons. // Please note that site may be accessible via http: or https:, but not both! $CFG -> sslproxy = true ; $CFG->reverseproxy is a different flag. It skips a wwwroot sanity check for load-balanced frontends. Turn both on and Moodle can refuse with “Reverse proxy enabled so the server cannot be accessed directly.” For TLS offload on a single public hostname, sslproxy is the one.

articles.title: 1 light-day from Earth! NASA's Voyager 1 probe hits huge milestone in interstellar space
articles.excerpt: It now takes 24 hours for even a single particle of light to reach Voyager.
articles.body: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is now one light-day from Earth — so far away that it takes signals a full 24 hours to reach the probe. Voyager 1 launched on Sept. 5, 1977, just a couple of weeks after Voyager 2 lifted off. But Voyager 1 launched on a faster trajectory than its twin and has just become the first spacecraft to ever reach one light-day away, which is equivalent to about 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), or the distance that one light particle travels in 24 hours. The milestone — which Voyager 1 hit today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) — shows the incredible ingenuity, technical ability and creativity from the teams at NASA that continue to innovate to keep this mission going nearly five decades later.

articles.title: NASA Launches Nuclear Power Systems Student Contest
articles.excerpt: NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the Un…
articles.body: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source. Some of the most interesting locations to study on our Moon face some of the harshest conditions.
